abstract_primary: Across 28 matched initialization dates and 12,096 twelve-site queries, mean compatible probability widths were 0.1407 / 0.0885 / 0.0142 in that release order; 3,941 reference tails were zero, 3,469 were one, and 5,064 queries had at most two uncertain sites. The 2,871 prespecified informative queries had widths 0.5139 / 0.3146 / 0.0547; pairs numerically identified 1,068 tails and the aggregate captured 43.4% of marginal-to-pair narrowing. Across illustrative cost–loss ratios 0.1, 0.25 and 0.5, margins certified 85.9%–87.8% of all 12,096 queries at each ratio, versus 91.4%–92.0% for the aggregate and 98.4%–99.5% for pairs. Among informative queries within 0.1 of those thresholds (N=532 / 693 / 623, in cost-ratio order), certification ranged from 0.2%–2.3% for margins, 7.2%–15.0% for the aggregate and 74.7%–91.0% for pairs. At ratio 0.1 the informative filter itself fixes a weakly optimal action; certification uses only released moments.
abstract_sensitivity: Pair near-identification is conditional on exact moments of the fifty-member empirical law. With 10 / 25 / 50 members, informative-stratum pair widths were 0.0023 / 0.0219 / 0.0547 (N=3,176 / 2,726 / 2,871; the empirical laws and informative strata differ). In the fixed 120-query cohort, an arbitrary-weight moment allowance of 0.005 raised pair width from 0.0514 to 0.1858; these neighborhoods are not confidence sets. Compact and dispersed portfolios differ substantially; transfer to larger ensembles or other spacings was not tested.
abstract_exploratory: Exploratory controls distinguish interval ambiguity from midpoint error and show that the same 0.005 allowance changes no moment counts when exactly fifty equal-weight members are required. No observed-weather skill, health benefit, realized economic value or network saving was measured.
